thread:
olivia: Heads-up: Venatrix7B int4 onboarding is flapping on streaming tests. Single-shot looks fine but streaming outputs repeat a 4-token pattern around token 128-132 and sometimes drifts after 256. Perplexity +12% on summarization anchors.

sam: Hmm. Which converter/version + tokenizer did you use? Any special normalization?

olivia: Converted with modelx-convert v0.9.1 -> GGUF. Tokenizer source is venatrix_vocab.json (we normalize NFKC). Quant pipeline: quilta int4 with 1024 calib. Commands: 
```
modelx-convert --ckpt venatrix7b.ckpt --out venatrix.gguf --tokenizer venatrix_vocab.json --serialize-order legacy
quilta quantize --input venatrix.gguf --bits 4 --calibration 1024 --kernel permute
```
Observed soft-hyphen (U+00AD) and ZWJ (U+200D) in tokenizer mapped to ids 305/306 in original but converter output lists them as 306/305.

marta: If token ids swapped, streaming kv index will reference wrong cached positions. That explains incremental repeats but single-shot OK. Did you repro with `--preserve-token-ids`?

olivia: Not initially. I re-ran with preserve and the streaming duplication disappeared. But still saw minor rotary phase jitter on heads 6-7 in int4 artifacts — small token probability skew.

ravi: Could be headwise packing in the int4 kernel causing reordering that our rotary table selection assumes fixed token-id ordering for sentinel offsets. I'll diff the rotary tables and kvcache offsets from gguf vs converted with preserve.

ops-bot: CI: added a conversion toggle preserve_ids to the staging pipeline for venatrix-onboard.

sam: Triage plan: 1) Add incremental vs single-shot equality regression (32 anchors), 2) Add kv continuity check that validates streaming sequence == single-shot sequence, 3) Add headwise rotary-phase checksum per layer to catch head permute. If int4 divergence >7% ROUGE or >5% perplexity we fail.

marta: I'll prepare a minimal repro that demonstrates the id-swap -> streaming duplication with a short script. It should be small enough to attach to PR.

olivia: Example repro loop I used: 
```python
# stream_vs_one_shot.py (snip)
for prompt in anchors:
    single = gen(prompt, mode='single')
    stream = gen(prompt, mode='stream')
    assert stream.tokens == single.tokens, 'KV mismatch'
```
This fails on int4 w/out preserve flag.

ravi: I dumped layer 11 q/k matrices float32 vs int4 packing: saw a byte-offset shift for heads 4-7 in the int4 kernel ordering. That + token-id swap = double-indexing. I'll open converter patch to ensure tokenizer special token map preserved and add kernel-aware header for pack-order.

sam: Also log note: int8 path doesn't exhibit the bug, so int4 packing permutations expose latent ordering assumptions in converter + our streaming runtime glue.

olivia: Status update (1hr): Re-convert with preserve, re-quantize with quilta and kernel permute disabled. Streaming checks pass across anchors. ROUGE delta ~0.9%, perplexity delta ~1.2% vs fp32. Looks green.

marta: Good. After PR: we should add a conversion smoke test to onboarding checklist: verify special token id parity between original tokenizer and converted GGUF and run streaming equality gate.

ravi: I'll include binary repro artifacts and the layer q/k diffs in the PR. Also adding a unit that asserts rotary table head order matches kernel packing.

sam: I'll push the CI gates: 32 anchors, ROUGE threshold = 5% (fail), kv continuity must be exact.

olivia: Ok assigning: sam -> CI gate + threshold; ravi -> PR + repro artifacts; marta -> small repro script + doc snippet; olivia -> update onboarding ticket and mark Venatrix int4 blocked until CI green. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
